chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Shuqran, the slave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), cast the cotton spread upon him in his grave.

key_terms.شُقْرَانُ: Shuqran, a slave of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What was placed on the Prophet Muhammad in his grave according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi records the specific burial practice of placing a cotton spread (qatifah) over the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) by his slave Shuqran, highlighting the reverence shown even in the immediate interment. It serves as a foundational reference for Shia jurisprudence regarding the leveling of the grave (lahad) and the modesty of the Prophet's resting place, distinguishing it from later elaborate structures.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The cotton spread was cast upon Shuqran, a slave of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, in his grave’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Husayn ibn ‘Uthman from ibn Muskan from Aban ibn Taghlib who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘
Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, placed bricks on the grave of the Holy prophet.’ I then asked, ‘If one places tiles on the grave is it harmful to the deceased?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not harmful.’”
